title: North train coming into Hartland station
description: The express passenger train nears the Hartland Train Station, preparing to cross Orser Street. The building on the left was originally built as a hotel and saloon for railroad workers, later housing a variety of businesses. By the time it burned in 1960, it served as Jim Lavigne’s residence, pool hall, and barber shop. The cement block building on the right became the first office of the Observer newspaper, founded by Fred Stevens.
